name: Guaibasaurus
isnote: Most analyses recover it as a sauropodomorph, but some suggest a theropod; Bonaparte et al. (1999) found it a possible basal theropod and gave it its own family (Wikipedia revision); PBDB places it in Guaibasauridae.
sum: Guaibasaurus is a small basal saurischian from the Late Triassic Caturrita Formation of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, usually recovered as a sauropodomorph.
wsnote: 2 m and 10 kg (G. S. Paul) to 3 m and 35 kg (Molina-Pérez and Larramendi 2020), as quoted by the cited Wikipedia revision.
holotype: MCN PV2355, a well-preserved partial postcranial skeleton.
material: Two further specimens, UFRGS PV0725T (a nearly complete postcranial skeleton lacking one forelimb, both feet and the neck) and MCN PV 10112 (a block with articulated and isolated elements).
biology: One skeleton lies in a posture like the resting position of birds, otherwise known mainly from maniraptoran dinosaurs.
author: Bonaparte et al. 1999
